business_quality_reasoning: Trading since 1983 as AMP Electric Contractors Ltd, 5.0 stars across 24 reviews, OZEV-approved EV charge point installer under a government scheme, covering commercial and domestic work with 24/7 emergency call-outs. A long-established, high-trust operation with higher-value job types.
price_point_reasoning: Services include EV charge point installations (typically £800-1,500), full/partial rewires and safety certification; £800 is a reasonable midpoint job value.
modernity_gap: A dark, letter-spaced GoDaddy builder site with a 2020 copyright and an announcement popup blocking the entire page on load — looks and behaves like a site untouched for 5+ years.
site_weaknesses: A full-screen 'Announcement' popup about EV charging blocks the homepage on both desktop and mobile before a visitor sees anything
Services are presented as a centred bold bullet list with no imagery, detail or pricing guidance
No reviews or testimonials shown anywhere despite a 5.0 Google rating
Accreditation badges (NICEIC, Part P, OZEV) are reduced to tiny icons at the very bottom of the page
Letter-spaced uppercase text and the heavy dark theme make the copy hard to scan
Contact form is generic with an 'Attach Files' option but no service selection or quote framing
site_analysis: The business has real depth — decades of trading, OZEV approval for EV charger installs, emergency call-outs — but the site actively gets in its own way: a popup covers the whole homepage on arrival, and the content behind it is a plain services list with no proof, no reviews and no personality. A visitor has to work hard to discover why they should call.
review_summary: Your business has credentials most competitors would envy — OZEV approval, NICEIC registration and 24-hour emergency cover — but your website hides nearly all of it. Visitors are greeted by a popup announcement before they can even see your page, and there is not a single review on the site despite your 5-star Google rating. Clearing these obstacles would let your reputation do the selling.
outreach_angle: You've been trading since 1983 and you're OZEV-approved for EV chargers, but the first thing a visitor sees on your site is a popup covering the whole page — the site is hiding your strongest selling points.
